summary: Enichi Ocho was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo around 1926–1929. He later served as professor emeritus at Otani University, attested between 1972 and 1979.

Enryo Inoue was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Higashi Hongan-ji, Niigata Prefectural Nagaoka High School, and the University of Tokyo (~1881–1885). He founded Toyo University, holding posts there (~1887–1906) and at Keihoku Gakuen Hakusan High School (~1899–1906).

Ensho Kanakura was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1917–1920). He held posts at Tohoku University (1923–1987), Rissho University (~1958–1976), Miyagi University of Education (1968–1974), and the Japan Academy (~1970–1987).
Ensho Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Eshō Mikogami and earned a PhD at Ryukoku University, attested in 1996.

Enshu Kurumiya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a Ph.D. at the Australian National University by 1974 and served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University, attested between 1981 and 1985.

Erberto Lo Bue was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who earned a Ph.D. at SOAS University of London (~1976–1981). He served as a lecturer at the University of Milan (~1988–1997) and held a post at the University of Bologna (~1997–2011).

Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University, attested in 2003. He studied under doctoral supervisors Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton, as well as several other teachers.
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Manchester (~1955–1958). He held posts at Manchester (~1965–1970), Lancaster University (~1970–1977), and the University of Sydney as First Chair of Religious Studies (1977–1996).

Eric M. Greene is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his PhD at UC Berkeley by 2012 under Robert H. Sharf and other teachers. Attested in 2017, he served as assistant professor of religious studies at Yale University.
Eric Reinders is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned master's degrees from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia (attested 2012), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

Erich Frauwallner was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Vienna (1918–1921). He held professorial and emeritus posts at the University of Vienna between 1955 and 1974.

Erich Haenisch was a scholar of sinology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts at Leipzig University (~1925–1932), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1945), University of Göttingen (~1945–1946), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1946–1952).

Erich Rudolf Jaensch was a scholar of philosophy who held academic posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from approximately 1910 to 1913 and at the University of Marburg from approximately 1913 to 1940.
Erik Braun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso, along with Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun.

Erik Haarh was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who earned a doctor's degree at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1969). He held a post at the Royal Danish Library from approximately 1957 to 1974.

Erik J. Hammerstrom is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a Doctor of Philosophy from Indiana University. He served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University, attested in 2016.

Erik Zürcher was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1947–1959), studying under Paul Demiéville, Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, and others. He served as Professor of East Asian History at Leiden (1961–1993).

Erik-Jan Zürcher is a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Het Rijnlands Lyceum Oegstgeest (~1965–1971) and Leiden University (~1971–1984), later holding a post at Leiden University from approximately 1997 to 2018.
